method: Permanent PDF redaction plus source-qualified correction panels; unchanged original pages retained. Clinical source gaps are not interpreted as false claims.

updates.text: The 0.95% annual rupture estimate belongs to UCAS Japan. It is a cohort estimate, not a shared ISUIA/UCAS rate or an individual prediction. Across-study ranges depend on population and aneurysm characteristics.
Third-nerve palsy may be pupil-involving or pupil-sparing. Pupil sparing does not exclude an aneurysm or another compressive cause; it should not be used as a rule-out shortcut.

updates.text: Randomized modality evidence exists. CURES randomized 291 participants to surgery or endovascular treatment: treatment failure was 9% versus 19%, mainly angiographic; mRS >2 at 1 year was 2% in both groups. TEAM stopped because of poor recruitment. These do not settle preventive intervention versus observation for every unruptured aneurysm.

Observational complication comparisons do not establish universal endovascular superiority. Treatment depends on anatomy, patient risk and multidisciplinary judgment. The reproduced surgical forest plot contains a source-level diabetes/HTN row inconsistency; that row is withheld. The article text reports diabetes OR 2.38 (95% CI 1.54-3.67), while 1.45 (1.03-2.03) belongs to hypertension.

Intention-to-treat analysis preserves randomized allocation despite crossover or nonadherence. It does not mean ignoring missing outcomes or treating complete-case analysis as unbiased; prespecified handling of missing data and sensitivity analyses are essential.

The Bailey trial enrolled sciatica lasting 4-12 months. Prior surgery at the involved lumbar level was an exclusion; do not broaden that to every prior lumbosacral operation. Its primary pain outcome was assessed at 6 months.
The stroke-subtype proportions reproduced from AHA/ASA 2021 Figure 1 are approximate and vary with population and diagnostic testing.

Distinguish observed associations from causality. The displayed HDL genetic association (nominal P=.031) did not meet the study’s multiple-testing threshold; LDL was not associated in that analysis. This does not establish that LDL-lowering treatment lacks clinical benefit.

The right-hand list combines heterogeneous reported presentations and lesion locations. These are not each validated markers of lacunar small-vessel disease; a clinical syndrome alone does not establish its mechanism.
Capsular warning syndrome describes recurrent, stereotyped crescendo episodes; a single preceding TIA is not sufficient to establish it.
Original INO illustration: panel A (patient 7) is ischemic infarction; panel B (patient 19) is demyelination. The images illustrate the differential and must not both be labeled lacunar infarction.

The incomplete 2020 acute-treatment algorithm has been retired. Current reperfusion decisions require treatment-specific time, clinical and imaging criteria and appropriate stroke-unit care. The retained AHA 2021 diagram concerns secondary-prevention evaluation: a clinical TIA merits comparable etiologic evaluation even without a visible infarct, with appropriate basic laboratory testing.

updates.text: Multiple acute lesions increase suspicion for an alternative source; they do not prove embolism. STRIVE dimensions are approximate axial conventions, not stand-alone diagnostic cutoffs. A lacune is a cavity with additional imaging features; clinical small-vessel events may lack a visible DWI lesion.

Diagnosis integrates a compatible clinical event, imaging and exclusion of plausible alternatives. Risk factors support the assessment but are not obligatory; a visible single-perforator lesion is not required in every clinical lacunar event.
Thrombus extension, branch occlusion, hemodynamic failure and edema are proposed mechanisms of progression. The list does not establish a mechanism-directed treatment with proven benefit.

Short-course DAPT applies to selected acute noncardioembolic minor stroke/high-risk TIA, with initiation, duration and reperfusion exclusions specified by current guidance. The CHANCE single-acute-infarction subgroup is not synonymous with lacunar disease; the adjacent monotherapy-versus-placebo meta-analyses do not test DAPT versus monotherapy.

Original-source inconsistency: SPS3 Figure 1 baseline risk-set labels show placebo 1517 and clopidogrel 1503, whereas Tables 1-3 report placebo 1503 and clopidogrel 1517. The figure is retained as a historical reproduction with this explicit caveat; no inference is made that later risk-set counts are also wrong.

Lipid treatment should follow the patient’s atherosclerotic/ASCVD risk and current guidance. The 2021 LDL-C <70 mg/dL recommendation specifically concerns stroke/TIA with atherosclerotic disease; SPARCL tested atorvastatin 80 mg, not randomized LDL targets. This is not a reason to withhold indicated statin treatment.
The figure describes late functional improvement in selected 3-month survivors. It is not a universal lacunar recovery trajectory or a reason to defer rehabilitation.

HOMA-IR = fasting glucose (mmol/L) × fasting insulin (microU/mL) / 22.5; with glucose in mg/dL, the denominator is 405. IRIS used >3 as a study-selection cutoff, not a universal diagnosis; assay calibration and fasting timing matter. Prediabetes associations vary by definition: fasting glucose 100-125 mg/dL alone had RR 1.08 (95% CI 0.94-1.23) in the cited meta-analysis.

updates.text: The recurrence/vascular-event curves concern 1008 patients with first ischemic stroke at ages 15-49, including 44 with type 1 and 60 with type 2 diabetes. Their 10-year risks are not general estimates for all stroke survivors. Unpaired curve cells remain historical source values, not independently verified individual predictions.

Hyperglycemia estimates depend on threshold and timing: about 40% had admission random glucose >=130 mg/dL in a 656-patient single-center AIS cohort. Continuous monitoring in a separate 59-patient cohort showed substantial change over time. Fixed diabetes/non-diabetes percentages are not universal prevalence estimates.

region_replacements.text: Prevalence depends on threshold and timing. See source context below.

updates.text: DCCT/EDIC studied type 1 diabetes (1441 participants) with long-term follow-up. The cardiovascular outcome was a composite; the small cerebrovascular event counts (1 versus 5) do not establish a separately powered stroke effect.

IRIS enrolled age >=40, stroke/TIA within 6 months, HbA1c <7% and HOMA-IR >3 measured with fasting sampling at least 14 days after the event. Heart-failure and bladder-cancer/risk exclusions, gradual dose escalation and safety monitoring matter. Serious fractures requiring hospitalization or surgery occurred in 5.1% versus 3.2%; the reproduced other-fracture row of 6.9% versus 4.9% is a different adverse-event category.

For most stable secondary-prevention patients, BP <130/80 mmHg is appropriate when tolerated. Regimen choice is individualized and includes thiazide/thiazide-like diuretics as well as selected ACE inhibitors, ARBs or calcium-channel blockers. This does not specify acute-stroke BP management.

Current LDL goals depend on risk: 2026 guidance uses <55 mg/dL for very-high-risk clinical ASCVD, alongside >=50% reduction and indicated nonstatin therapy. Stroke plus diabetes alone does not automatically meet every very-high-risk definition. Other clinical-ASCVD patients may retain a <70 goal.

In the ARISTOTLE diabetes analysis, relative stroke/systemic-embolism, mortality and intracranial-bleeding benefits were broadly similar, but major-bleeding reduction differed (interaction P=.003), favoring a larger reduction without diabetes. Do not generalize one endpoint or one DOAC to identical efficacy and risks across all groups.

Historical outlook updated: selected GLP-1-based therapies now have established cardiovascular indications in appropriate patients, independent of HbA1c. Lipidomic and mechanistic questions remain research topics; do not group established outcome therapies with wholly experimental strategies.

SHINE found no 90-day functional benefit and more hypoglycemia with intensive acute insulin. Older type 2 diabetes intensity trials did not demonstrate a significant stroke reduction; DCCT/EDIC concerned long-term type 1 cardiovascular outcomes. These are distinct from modern drug-specific cardiovascular benefits.

The Friedewald TG/5 equation requires mg/dL concentrations (use TG/2.2 with mmol/L). It should not be used with TG >=400 mg/dL; the 2026 guideline prefers Martin/Hopkins or Sampson/NIH estimation where appropriate.
ApoB100 occurs on VLDL, IDL and LDL. Chylomicron remnants contain ApoB48; distinguish these isoforms from a total ApoB measurement.

Northern Manhattan Study: HDL-C >=35 mg/dL, not <=35, was associated with adjusted OR 0.53 (95% CI 0.39-0.72) for ischemic stroke (539 cases, 905 controls). The reproduced secondary table inherited the reversed threshold; that row has been removed.

The unverified historical lipid-percentage treatment table has been retired. Biochemical lipid changes are not equivalent to evidence of stroke-outcome benefit; choose therapy using current indication-specific outcome evidence.

updates.text: This was an observational study of 163 patients with ICH. It associated statin exposure with cortico-subcortical microbleeds (OR 4.15, 95% CI 1.54-11.20); it does not demonstrate recurrent lobar hemorrhage or statin causation.

OSLER was an open-label extension (n=4465, median 11.1 months). Its cardiovascular result was exploratory (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.28-0.78), alongside LDL lowering. It should not stand alone as current definitive cardiovascular-outcome evidence.

The 2013/2014 prescribing algorithms have been retired. Use current risk-stratified lipid guidance. After ICH, AHA/ASA 2022 states that the balance of statin risks and benefits for ICH outcomes/recurrence versus cardiovascular prevention is uncertain (Class IIb, B-NR); this is not an automatic stop or continue rule.

updates.text: Lp(a) measurement at least once in adults and selected ApoB assessment are established roles in 2026 guidance. Lp-PLA2 and HDL-subfraction testing remain separate investigational questions.

The displayed Lp-PLA2 activity estimate per 30 nmol/min/mL was HR 1.07 (95% CI 1.01-1.13). After adjustment for LDL, it attenuated to 1.04 (0.97-1.11); this limits an independent-marker interpretation.

Statins reduce recurrent vascular risk in appropriate atherosclerotic/ASCVD populations. This should not be generalized to an identical indication after every cerebral-ischemia mechanism; apply the patient’s current risk and indication.

This is a historical research outlook. Current evidence now includes nonstatin outcome therapies and an established Lp(a) screening role; remaining lipidomic, population and cognitive questions should be identified separately as research.

This timeline is historical and not a standardized comparison of benefits. ACT I established noninferiority within a prespecified margin; a nonsignificant comparison is not proof of equivalence. Trials used different endpoints, procedural windows and medical treatment.

ACAS medical care included aspirin and risk-factor management. CREST-1 safety rates 2.5% versus 1.4% refer to its asymptomatic subgroup. ACT I met noninferiority. ACST-2: 5-year nonprocedural stroke 5.3% versus 4.5%; procedural stroke/death 3.7% versus 2.7% among patients who underwent the procedure. ECST-2 primary hierarchical win ratio 1.01 (95% CI 0.60-1.70); its 10.5%/10.2% pair was secondary, and the unsupported 1.2% safety estimate is removed. SPACE-2 used an ECST stenosis threshold and a perioperative/later ipsilateral composite.

The annual percentage changes describe standardized utilization per 100,000 population, not raw procedure volumes. The asymptomatic proportion derives from four state databases with differing coverage periods.
The AF exclusion was atrial fibrillation prompting anticoagulation, not every AF diagnosis. Interpret the eligibility diagram with the complete original criteria.

The WHO symptom-duration boundary is at least 24 hours. Secondary tissue-based outcomes were defined composites including specified infarction/hemorrhage and death components, with territory and time-window limits; they are not a count of routine MRI lesions alone.
Broadly similar measured risk-factor control does not establish absence of performance bias in an open-label trial. Masked endpoint adjudication is a separate design feature.

The WHO clinical symptom-duration boundary is at least 24 hours (>=24h), not more than 24 hours. The misleading MRI-infarction row is withheld pending exact secondary-composite/appendix reconciliation. The main report’s tissue-based composites include specified death and cerebral infarction/hemorrhage components and cannot be labeled routine MRI lesions.

For CEA, the reported tipping analysis required at least 7 events removed from the CEA arm or at least 6 added to the medical arm to cross the significance boundary. Changing statistical significance does not nullify or reverse an observed treatment effect.

The approximate NNT of 31 is for the 4-year primary composite, including perioperative death, not stroke alone. High-risk plaque features are prognostic observational findings; they are not a validated rule identifying who specifically benefits from CAS.

updates.text: Near-occlusion with distal collapse and complete occlusion are different anatomical categories. They must not be treated as synonyms.
The ACES curves concern asymptomatic >=70% carotid stenosis with two-year follow-up. Their absolute risks should not be transferred to recently symptomatic disease.

The POINT carotid subgroup excluded planned carotid revascularization. A nonsignificant interaction does not prove equal DAPT benefit between stenosis groups. CARESS tested a microembolic-signal surrogate, not clinical stroke reduction.

LDL goals are risk-specific: <55 mg/dL for very-high-risk ASCVD in 2026 guidance; <70 remains relevant in other atherosclerotic secondary-prevention settings. Icosapent eligibility depends on triglycerides, background statin therapy and relevant comorbidities; it is not a universal response to any hypertriglyceridemia.

The vascular evidence here is pioglitazone-specific, not a thiazolidinedione class effect; selected poststroke insulin-resistant patients require heart-failure/bladder-cancer risk assessment and adverse-effect monitoring. Individualize glycemic goals and avoid hypoglycemia; tighter HbA1c targets have not been established as recurrent-stroke treatment.

Routine CEA/CAS is not recommended for symptomatic near-occlusion with distal collapse. ESVS 2023 allows consideration after multidisciplinary review when recurrent carotid-territory symptoms persist despite best medical therapy; evidence is weak. Complete occlusion is a different category.

Routine CEA/CAS is not recommended for symptomatic near-occlusion with distal collapse. ESVS 2023 allows consideration after multidisciplinary review when recurrent carotid-territory symptoms persist despite best medical therapy; evidence is weak. Complete occlusion is a different category.

Timely CEA benefits selected recently symptomatic patients. A blanket ban on intervention in the first 2 days is incorrect: ESVS permits urgent CEA, preferably within 24 hours, for selected stroke-in-evolution or crescendo-TIA patients. Large/disabling infarction or altered consciousness instead supports deferral and specialist assessment.

Observational comparisons found lower in-hospital stroke/death with TCAR than transfemoral CAS, with more access complications requiring intervention. These are not randomized proof of equivalence to CEA or universally lower TCAR risk.

updates.text: For dominant proximal M2 occlusion, AHA/ASA 2026 considers EVT reasonable within 6 hours in selected patients with prestroke mRS 0-1, NIHSS >=6 and ASPECTS >=6 (Class IIa, B-NR). Proximal OR dominant M2 plus salvageable tissue is not the complete recommendation. Other vessel recommendations have their own eligibility criteria.

THALES: NIHSS <=5, or high-risk TIA with ABCD2 >=6 or symptomatic stenosis >=50%. CHANCE moderate/severe hemorrhage was 7 (0.3%) versus 8 (0.3%); the separate hazard-ratio cell remains source-limited. Do not assign CHANCE/POINT eligibility to THALES. INSPIRES enrolled selected patients with presumed atherosclerotic origin; clinical eligibility differed for <=24 versus 24-72 hours. A general <=72-hour label is not the complete enrollment rule.

updates.text: OCEANIC-STROKE required at least one of nonlacunar infarct, history of atherosclerosis or cerebrovascular atherosclerotic plaque. Major bleeding 1.9% versus 1.7%, HR 1.10 (95% CI 0.85-1.44), does not establish absence of every bleeding effect. CSPS.com required MRI-confirmed high-risk noncardioembolic stroke with >=50% intracranial OR extracranial stenosis, OR at least two specified risk factors; ICAD was not universal.

updates.text: ANGEL-ASPECT protocol: NIHSS 6-30; ASPECTS 3-5 without a core-volume restriction; ASPECTS <3 with core 70-100 mL within 24 hours; or ASPECTS >5 with core 70-100 mL at 6-24 hours. These trial criteria are distinct from current EVT guidance.
SELECT2 correction: the proportion meeting both ASPECTS <=5 and core >=50 mL was 66.8%, not 78%. This source correction does not change the direction or significance of the main treatment result.

BASICS crossover: 3/154 assigned EVT received medical treatment only, and 7/146 assigned medical treatment received EVT. The 29.2% figure concerns eligible patients treated outside the trial. Subgroup findings were descriptive, underpowered and not multiplicity-adjusted; the proximal-basilar interval crossed 1.

BASICS crossover: 3/154 assigned EVT received medical treatment only, and 7/146 assigned medical treatment received EVT. The 29.2% figure concerns eligible patients treated outside the trial. Subgroup findings were descriptive, underpowered and not multiplicity-adjusted; the proximal-basilar interval crossed 1.

ATTENTION historical trial selection: age <80 years required pc-ASPECTS >=6 and prestroke mRS 0-2; age >=80 years required pc-ASPECTS >=8 and prestroke mRS 0. The trial also required NIHSS >=10 and randomization within 12 hours of estimated basilar-artery occlusion. These historical entry criteria are not current stand-alone EVT eligibility rules.

Trial populations must remain separate: WAKE-UP studied MRI DWI-FLAIR mismatch of unknown onset and excluded planned EVT; EPITHET did not require mismatch in every participant; EXTEND allowed CT or MRI perfusion and wake-up midpoint selection. CHABLIS-TII included large/medium occlusions and used a 24-48-hour reperfusion-without-sICH endpoint, unlike 90-day functional outcomes. HOPE used core <=70 mL, ratio >=1.2 and mismatch >=10 mL. Unqualified cross-trial NNT/NNH and population-to-benefit shortcuts are removed; nonsignificant safety differences do not establish harm.

updates.text: Coma is not an assessable delirium state. Persistent coma was excluded from the original CAM-ICU validation. Language-dependent attention tasks can be confounded by aphasia; interpret attention, arousal and language jointly rather than using the table as a binary diagnosis.
